cells.tense: You are standing where the pattern gets established and you can gather what might be felt.
cells.act: work the pattern through to its logic
cells.ask: Settle an offer you're weighing into the structure you're building. Say where it belongs, then don't touch it again this week.
cells.core:
You can feel what a group might become without sinking into it, and you're often the one who puts the shape around it — the standing slot, the regular time, the way things get done here. The shape holds because you kept feeling out what was possible in it, and nothing has to be frozen for you to stand in a crowd and let it come together.

The pull still spends itself on what's next, so it would rather keep every option open than lay a working shape over one. Settle an offer you're weighing into the structure you're building — say where it belongs, then don't touch it again this week. What you set down holds. By next week there's something the others can stand in.
cells.sheetLine: You can build the shape and keep feeling for more at once.
cells.place: where you establish the pattern things run on

cells.tense: You are bracing against a future that can't be written in yet, still gathering what might be felt.
cells.ask: Nothing new enters for seven days. What's already started gets the next move, and whatever else arrives waits its turn.
cells.core:
Where you set the pattern, not much is landing. Every new person at the table is another option to keep open, every fresh offer one more thing to see before anything finishes. You're not confused — you're gathering, the way you do at the start of making. But the gathering keeps moving on, and the ones who came to stand in what you built keep watching the exits rather than the thing itself.

Nothing new enters for seven days. What's already started gets the next move, and whatever else arrives waits its turn. That's what makes a form hold — it stays the thing at hand instead of the next one. The rest can keep being possible. What you already began gets to finish.
cells.sheetLine: Nothing settles because everything is still possible.
cells.place: where you establish the pattern things run on

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed behind you, where the pattern gets established.
cells.act: let the mind rest instead of working the problem
cells.ask: Leave the problem on the desk one afternoon and go out with no errand. Don't fix anything; just watch where you end up.
cells.core:
Where you establish the pattern, not much new is getting let in. You run what already runs, you keep the shape you inherited, and the pull toward what might be felt doesn't get much say. The structure stands. The feeling isn't being drawn.

Leave the problem on the desk one afternoon and go out with no errand. Don't fix anything; just watch where you end up. What you're after isn't a better structure — it's someone beside you, and that only shows when you stop working the shape for a bit. The structure holds itself. You can leave it standing and go find out who's in it.
cells.sheetLine: The structure stands, and nothing new gets drawn into it.

cells.tense: You are choosing what might be felt and filing the choosing under the room's mood, not yours.
cells.act: cut through the story to what actually follows
cells.ask: Put a rule you keep here on the table and write what it really protects. Keep the page to yourself.
cells.core:
You gather what might be felt and build the pattern around it, then call that reading the room. The choices about who gets what are happening, and they come from your eye and your way of arranging things — the standing slot, the regular time, the shape that holds. The people using it don't file it that way.

Put a rule you keep here on the table and write what it really protects. Not why you made it — what it keeps standing. Keep the page to yourself. No one has to be told. But it puts your name back on the shaping that's underway, and what you decide next lands differently once you can see the pattern is yours.
cells.sheetLine: You call the room's shape a mood, and it isn't.
cells.place: where you establish the pattern things run on

A reader could reasonably say the Too Much cell flatters the person's taste, so it names the leaving and the unwatched options rather than the eye. Every ask is still useful if the read is wrong: laying a structure over a gathered offer, putting one down finished, resting long enough to read the frame, and asking what one line actually is are all good moves in a wrong reading. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person was the image of everything on the table with nothing served — cut it to plain leaving what leaves.
